doc: The kernel's commands, by number (@xpute/core/abi/cmd.ts: `major << 8 | minor`),
and the packet each carries — an XTP branch whose children are its fields, in
order. A command with no fields carries no packet. The kernel is the process; the
JavaScript around it is two things to it, its host, which holds the devices and
the turns, and its shell, the UI. The commands are grouped by which of them a
command is between.
The same number is a command on the submission ring and a signal on the
completion ring (its `RES` clear). The direction is the ring: `packet` is
what the shell submits, `signal` what the kernel posts. Each is written and
read by what this file generates, on both sides, so no field is found by
its position anywhere else.
A field is a number of a width, a `bool`, a `str`, a member of an enum
below or of one another spec declares (`extern`), or a record below. An
`optional` one may be absent, its kind kept; a `list` is a branch of them,
or a packed array where the item is a number. A record crosses as a branch
of its own fields, and is how a block past a slot is laid out. An enum's
`unknown` is the member a number it does not give out reads as; an enum
without one refuses the packet.

extern.name: BakeKind
doc: By its index in BAKE_KINDS (published.spec.ts).

extern.name: SettingKey
doc: A setting by its place in schema.json's SETTINGS, its row's `key`.

extern.name: CharacterGroup
doc: variant.json's group, by its number.

extern.name: GroundChannelKey
doc: A ground channel by its identity (cube_type.json).

enums.name: Major
doc: What a command is about.

enums.name: WorldMinor
doc: The world's verbs.

enums.name: InputMinor
doc: The input's verbs: the canvas, the pointer, the map controls.

enums.name: SensorMinor
doc: The device sensors' verbs.

enums.name: ImageMinor
doc: An image's verbs.

enums.name: GpuMinor
doc: The GPU's verbs.

enums.name: SurfaceMinor
doc: A surface's verbs.

enums.name: SettingMinor
doc: A setting's verbs.

enums.name: ChatMinor
doc: The chat's verbs.

enums.name: PreviewMinor
doc: A preview's verbs.

enums.name: ProfilerMinor
doc: The profiler's verbs.

enums.name: PointerPhase
doc: Where a pointer event is in its gesture.

enums.name: PointerKind
doc: What the pointer is, as the browser's `pointerType` says.

enums.name: ActiveTool
doc: What the pointer holds.

enums.name: Tracking
doc: What the tracking button did, as the button showed it.

entries.name: Recenter
doc: Back to the device.

entries.name: Follow
doc: Follow mode on, where the compass is listened to.

entries.name: Unfollow
doc: Follow mode off, north up again.

enums.name: CompassState
doc: The compass over the map (shell/ui/compass.rs), as the kernel decides it.

entries.name: Hidden
doc: The map is north up, near enough.

entries.name: Shown
doc: The map is turned; a press turns it north up again.

entries.name: Following
doc: The map follows the device's heading: shown for where north is, dimmed and taking no press, since north up is the tracking button's to ask.

enums.name: GeolocationErrorCode
doc: The browser's PositionError codes.

enums.name: Sensor
doc: Which of the device's sensors.

enums.name: PermissionAnswer
doc: A sensor permission, as the shell's prompt or the browser's change reported it.

entries.name: Asking
doc: The shell's prompt is up.

entries.name: Failed
doc: The prompt itself threw.

enums.name: MapStatus
doc: The map's loading lifecycle.

enums.name: DevicePoseStatus
doc: Where a sensor's reading is: none asked for, asked for, arriving, failed, or none to be had, the device having no such sensor.

enums.name: Message
doc: A message the kernel raises and the shell shows.
The kernel decides which message a state calls for and carries the number.
It never carries the words: a string that exists to be read has no reason
to sit in the kernel's memory, and the shell has the locale files already
(apps/web/src/locale) — the same split `strerror` is on the other side of.
The number is the name here. A band is what a message is about, and a
message keeps its number for as long as anything can be holding one: an
old shell reads a number a new kernel sends, so a number that has meant
something must never come to mean another thing. Retire one by leaving
the gap.

entries.section: 0x02 where the device says it is
0x03 which way the device is facing
the process asks the host: its system calls, raised on the completion ring and run before the next turn (the rest are the host stream's records, host.json)

entries.name: SENSOR_START
doc: Start watching.

entries.name: SENSOR_STOP
doc: Stop watching.

entries.section: the host answers: an I/O the process started, done

entries.name: IMAGE_DECODED
doc: An image the kernel asked decoded (host.json's IMAGE_DECODE): 0, held for the renderer
as the kernel's `image`, or -errno where the file is not an image the device decodes.
A file that did not come is the open's answer (xpute's SYS_OPENED), not this.

entries.name: SENSOR_POSITION
doc: A GPS fix; a field is absent where the browser gave none.

entries.name: SENSOR_ORIENTATION
doc: An orientation event; a field is absent where the browser gave none.

entries.name: SENSOR_ERROR
doc: The watch failed and was stopped.

entries.name: SENSOR_ORIENTATION_LOST
doc: The compass failed and its listener was removed, where the platform says so.

entries.section: the host tells the process: its start, its turn, its window, its devices and its input

entries.name: WORLD_BOOT
doc: The kernel's start: what the platform is, and what it was handed to start with.

packet.name: development
doc: A development build, which offers the settings schema.json marks `dev`.

packet.name: orientation_permission
doc: iOS 13+'s gate: requestPermission exists and must run inside a gesture.

packet.name: orientation_silence_is_loss
doc: A browser's compass talks while the device is still and cannot say it stopped, so
silence is the only sign of loss; a device's speaks only when the heading turns and
reports a failure itself (SENSOR_ORIENTATION_LOST).

packet.name: settings
doc: What storage keeps of the settings, as it keeps it, empty for none: the kernel's own file
(host.json's STORAGE_KEYS), handed over unread as a process is handed its environment,
which the kernel reads and from then on writes itself.

entries.name: WORLD_FRAME
doc: The frame of the turn the doorbell's quota rang in: the effects' turn, then the tick's
phases on what is left of the quota, the fetches within the credits. The turn leaves
its signals on the completion ring, drawn by the kernel.

packet.name: width
doc: The viewport, in CSS pixels.

packet.name: delta_s
doc: The frame interval and the turn, as the host measured them.

packet.name: unix_ms
doc: The local wall clock: `Date.now()`, the local hour, minute and second, and the local day's start.

entries.name: WORLD_VISIBILITY
doc: The tab's visibility; the host rings the doorbell for it at once, since a hidden
page gets no frame and hiding is the save's last sure moment.

entries.name: WORLD_SOURCE
doc: What the tile source declares of itself, once the shell has it (published.json's
SOURCE, or the dev tile server's answer in the same form). Until it comes nothing is
observed: the floor is held at the level it names, and no view is drawn from a
level the source does not supply whole.

packet.name: top_level
doc: The coarsest level of the pyramid the source supplies whole.

entries.name: SENSOR_PERMISSION
doc: A permission as the shell's prompt or the browser's change reported it.

entries.name: INPUT_RECT
doc: The canvas's client rect.

entries.name: INPUT_POINTER
doc: A pointer event on the canvas, in client pixels, with what the pointer holds; the
shell sends a move at the last position when the holding changes, as a browser
synthesizes a mouse move.

packet.name: channel
doc: The ground channel the held cube stands in for; absent for a flat color, a decor kind or nothing.

packet.name: value
doc: The held cube's type in its channel, or the decor kind, by the catalog's number; what the object store keeps is the kernel's to derive.

packet.name: tier
doc: The object size, by its index in the snapshot's object_sizes.

entries.name: GPU_READY
doc: A device answered; the kernel's renderer is made on it (crates/pxl/web/render/src/gpu/renderer.rs).

entries.name: GPU_LOST
doc: The device went away, and every object on it.

entries.section: the shell and the process: what the UI asks of it, and what it shows the UI

entries.name: SURFACE_OPEN
doc: A call, answered with the surface's handle, 0 refused: a canvas the shell hands over, drawn by the kernel alone from then on.

packet.name: role
doc: The renderer's surface_role (render/gpu/api.json).

entries.name: SURFACE_RESIZE
doc: The canvas's layout box in device pixels, transforms aside; the buffer it is drawn into is the kernel's.

entries.name: SURFACE_CLOSE
doc: A call: the canvas is going, and what it held on the device is let go before the call returns.

entries.name: PREVIEW_OPEN
doc: A character drawn alone into a surface the shell handed over, as the picker shows it.

entries.name: SETTING_SET
doc: A setting set from the sheet or the character picker.

packet.name: value
doc: A toggle's 0 or 1, a choice's option by its index, or a number.

entries.name: SETTING_TOGGLE
doc: A toggle's switch.

entries.name: CHAT_SEND
doc: A line the player said, shown over the character.

entries.name: INPUT_TRACKING
doc: The tracking button's press, as the button showed it.

entries.name: INPUT_VIEW
doc: Where the camera stands, set outright rather than driven: what the kernel's own
test puts a view at, and what an A/B reads two builds at the same view with.

entries.name: INPUT_RESET_DIST
doc: The scale bar's press: the default zoom.

entries.name: INPUT_COMPASS_RESET
doc: The compass's press: north up.

entries.name: INPUT_GO_TO
doc: A search result: the map center moved there.

entries.name: INPUT_POSE
doc: A tracked pose: where a tracker has the camera, and its turn as a unit quaternion
(x, y, z, w) from the camera's axes to the tracker's, in the world's units. The
first of a run is taken to be where the camera already is, so nothing moves as
it begins; the camera follows the tracker from there until POSE_END.

entries.name: INPUT_POSE_END
doc: The tracker let the camera go: back to the controller it had.

entries.name: SENSOR_OPEN
doc: The map is on screen and wants the sensors.

entries.name: SENSOR_CLOSE
doc: The map is gone, and the sensors are let go.

entries.name: SENSOR_ENABLE_LOCATION
doc: The search panel's location card: the location asked for. The compass is asked for
where it is used, entering follow mode (TRACKING), and never alone: nothing reads it
without the location.

entries.name: PROFILER_START
doc: A fresh recording window.

entries.name: PROFILER_STOP
doc: The window frozen, so what is exported holds still.

entries.name: PROFILER_LOG
doc: The console stream on or off.

entries.name: PROFILER_READ
doc: The profiler where it lies: the reply is the address of READ's words (profiler.json) over the
last `window_ms`, an infinite window being the whole recording, good until the next turn.

entries.name: PROFILER_TAKE
doc: The rows the console stream kept: the reply is the address of LOG's words, and the rows are let go on the next turn.

entries.name: WORLD_SNAPSHOT
doc: The UI's snapshot, when it changed: a Snapshot packet far past a ring frame, so a
block the kernel holds, valid until the next snapshot.

records.name: Snapshot
doc: What the page's UI shows of the kernel (shell/shell.rs): written after a turn that changed it, and replaced whole.

fields.name: azimuth
doc: The view's azimuth.

fields.name: zooming
doc: A zoom is in hand: two fingers are down, or a wheel's zoom is still arriving. The scale is shown while it is.

fields.name: settings
doc: Every setting's value by its SettingKey, as SETTING_SET carries one.

fields.name: place
doc: The place the map center is in, broad to narrow, already cut at the rung the
current zoom asks for; empty where the center is in none or the packets it is
read out of have not arrived.

fields.name: object_sizes
doc: The sizes an object places at, in units, coarsest first: the tiers the size flyout offers, one of which the shell holds by its index.

fields.name: center
doc: The map center in degrees: what the search measures distance from.

fields.name: page
doc: The L3 page the center falls in: what the area being looked at is announced per.
Sent because the shell would otherwise need a second implementation of the space
to reach it.

records.name: PlacePart
doc: One rung of the place, in every language the provider had rather than one resolved
name: the reader's language is the page's, and switching it re-reads a label already
sent.
